--- title: "[Graph.add_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add multiple edges to the graph in a single call. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L1580-L1781){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_edges( edges, rel=None, weight=None, auto_create_nodes=False, **shared_attrs, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Add several edges](/assets/graphs/add-edges.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: four nodes with two edges, B to A to C. After: two new edges, B to D and C to D, appear in the accent color in one call and close the cycle; no nodes are added." width="100%"} A bulk version of `add_edge()` that accepts a list of `(source, target)` pairs and applies shared attributes to all of them. A third element sets that edge's weight (a number) or overrides the shared attributes (a dict), so a weighted edge list reads like NetworkX's `add_weighted_edges_from()`: `[("A", "B", 2.0), ("B", "C", 0.5)]`. Endpoints are resolved exactly as in `add_edge()`: integers are node IDs and strings are node labels. Edges are added in list order, each with its own auto-assigned edge ID, and repeated pairs create parallel edges. The whole call is recorded as a single step in the step log (see `steps`). Typical uses: - wiring up a node set created with `add_nodes()` - building a graph directly from an edge list with `auto_create_nodes=True` - tagging a batch of edges with a common `rel=`, `weight=` or other attribute Every item's shape is checked before any edge is added, so a malformed item leaves the graph unchanged. Endpoints are only resolved while adding, though: if one can't be resolved part-way through the list, the edges before it have already been added when the error is raised. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edges]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Edge definitions to add. Each element can be: - `(source, target)`: shared attributes and `weight=` apply. - `(source, target, weight)`: a number (int, float or NumPy scalar) that sets this edge's weight, overriding `weight=`. - `(source, target, attrs_dict)`: the dict is merged on top of `**shared_attrs=` and may also contain `"rel"` and `"weight"` keys to override `rel=` and `weight=` for that edge. - `(source, target, weight, attrs_dict)`: both of the above. The dict must not also contain `"weight"`. Lists work in place of tuples. Any other shape (a bare string, a non-numeric, non-dict third element, or a different length) raises an error rather than being silently truncated. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional relationship type applied to every edge (unless overridden per-edge). Stored in the first-class `rel` column of the edge DataFrame. Default is `None`. [weight]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional numeric weight applied to every edge (unless overridden per-edge). As with `add_edge()`, the value is stored whether or not the graph was created with `weighted=True`. Default is `None` (no weight). [auto_create_nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, automatically create nodes for string labels that don't exist yet (integer IDs are never auto-created). If `False` (default), all referenced nodes must already exist. [**shared_attrs]{.doc-parameter-name} : Attributes applied to every edge (unless overridden per-edge), e.g., `color="gray"`. Each key becomes a column in the edge DataFrame. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns self to enable method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If an item isn't one of the accepted shapes (checked before any edge is added). [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If an item gives its weight both as the third element and in its dict, or if a source or target can't be resolved to an existing node (and `auto_create_nodes=` is `False`). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Add several edges at once between existing nodes: ::: {#c2951d64 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(['A', 'B', 'C', 'D']) .add_edges([('A', 'B'), ('B', 'C'), ('C', 'D')]) ) graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
shape: (3, 4)
idsourcetargetrel
i64i64i64null
112null
223null
334null
``` ::: ::: A shared relationship type is applied to every edge in the list: ::: {#fa429804 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(['Alice', 'Bob', 'Carol']) .add_edges( [('Alice', 'Bob'), ('Bob', 'Carol')], rel='follows' ) ) graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
shape: (2, 4)
idsourcetargetrel
i64i64i64str
112"follows"
223"follows"
``` ::: ::: A number as the third element is that edge's weight, which makes weighted edge lists compact: ::: {#e16828fb .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(weighted=True) .add_nodes(['A', 'B', 'C']) .add_edges([('A', 'B', 2.0), ('B', 'C', 0.5), ('A', 'C', 3.0)]) ) graph.get_edge_df().select(['source', 'target', 'weight']) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
shape: (3, 3)
sourcetargetweight
i64i64f64
122.0
230.5
133.0
``` ::: ::: A dict as the third tuple element overrides the shared values for that edge only. Here the A-C edge gets its own weight and `rel`, while A-B keeps the shared ones: ::: {#bd5e7a55 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True) .add_nodes(['A', 'B', 'C']) .add_edges( [ ('A', 'B'), ('A', 'C', {'weight': 2.0, 'rel': 'strong'}), ], rel='weak', weight=1.0 ) ) graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
shape: (2, 5)
idsourcetargetrelweight
i64i64i64strf64
112"weak"1.0
213"strong"2.0
``` ::: ::: With `auto_create_nodes=True`, a graph can be built straight from an edge list. The three people are created as nodes on the fly: ::: {#65bef1df .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_edges( [ ('Alice', 'Bob'), ('Bob', 'Carol'), ('Carol', 'Alice'), ], rel='knows', auto_create_nodes=True ) ) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` (3, 3) ``` ::: :::
